name: War Wound Veil

detectability.signature: Rotating energy curtain emitting polarized light in shifting violet and arterial red wavelengths

proximity: Ships experience intermittent power fluctuations as the vortex's energy field interacts with onboard systems
Visual sensors display a shimmering curtain of violet and red light rotating slowly in space
Crew report a persistent low-frequency vibration felt through deck plating
contact: Intense electromagnetic bombardment strips unshielded circuitry and fries exposed electronics
Energy currents within the vortex seize control of maneuvering thrusters, spinning vessels unpredictably
Biological crew suffer burns from ionized particle streams channeled along the vortex's rotation
prolonged_exposure: Complete systems failure as cascading electromagnetic interference overwhelms all redundancies
Cumulative radiation exposure causes deep-tissue damage and organ failure in biologicals
Ship hulls become magnetized, attracting debris and complicating future operations

age: Approximately 400 years, consistent with weapon discharge residue from the Palanquin Wars era

behavior.cycle: Completes a slow orbit around an empty point in space every 93 standard days

phenomena: The vortex orbits an apparently empty point in space where a planet or station may once have existed
Energy output intensifies when vessels approach, as though the vortex is responding to mass or power signatures
Debris caught in the vortex is slowly converted to ionized plasma, fueling the anomaly's continued existence
The violet-and-red color pattern matches the spectral signature of a weapon system used during the Palanquin Wars
hazards: The vortex's apparent responsiveness to approaching vessels makes safe observation distances unpredictable
Energy currents within the vortex can seize navigational control from even experienced pilots
Magnetized debris ejected from the vortex creates a hazardous field extending well beyond the visible boundary
opportunities: Study of the vortex's energy patterns provides insights into Palanquin-era weapon technology
The vortex's self-sustaining energy cycle is of intense interest to power generation researchers
Careful sampling of ionized debris within the vortex could reveal the composition of whatever was destroyed here
known_incidents: Archaeologist-pilot Senn Moire lost her port engine to the vortex's energy currents while attempting close-range spectral analysis, but recovered enough data to confirm the Palanquin Wars weapon signature
A pilgrim vessel from the Remembrance Compact deliberately entered the vortex in 3511 as an act of memorial; no survivors were recovered
description: The War Wound Veil is a rotating energy vortex approximately 4,200 kilometers across, emitting light in shifting curtains of deep violet and arterial red. It spins slowly in space, orbiting an empty point where spectral analysis suggests a substantial body—a planet, a station, or perhaps a fleet formation—once existed. The vortex's colors match the discharge signature of a directed-energy weapon system known to have been deployed during the Palanquin Wars, roughly four centuries ago.

The vortex behaves with an unsettling responsiveness. Its energy output measurably increases when vessels approach, with tendrils of ionized plasma extending toward the newcomer as though tasting the space around it. Ships that venture within the outer rotation are subject to electromagnetic bombardment and loss of navigational control as energy currents seize their thrusters. The vortex appears to be self-sustaining, converting any matter caught within it to ionized plasma that feeds back into the rotation.

The prevailing theory is that the War Wound Veil is the scar left by a catastrophic weapon discharge—a single, devastating strike that annihilated whatever occupied this point in space and left behind a self-perpetuating energy wound. The Palanquin Wars produced several such scars across the sector, but this is among the most energetic and best-preserved. The name reflects the widespread belief that this anomaly is not merely a phenomenon but a wound in space itself, one that has never healed.

The vortex is classified as a moderate navigation hazard with restricted approach protocols. A small research consortium studies it from a safe orbital distance, hoping to understand both the weapon that created it and the self-sustaining energy cycle that keeps it alive. Memorial groups from civilizations that fought in the Palanquin Wars occasionally visit the outer boundary to conduct remembrance ceremonies. The War Wound Veil endures as both a scientific curiosity and a monument to the destructive capacity of forgotten wars.
